pests.name: Subterranean Termites
pests.blurb: Eastern subterranean termites nest in sandy soil and run mud tubes up block and stucco to hit framing. They don't need much, just soil contact and damp mulch.

pests.name: Formosan Termites
pests.blurb: Formosans build huge colonies and they'll nest right in a wall void or soffit if AC condensation keeps it damp.

pests.name: Drywood Termites
pests.blurb: West Indian drywood termites don't use soil at all. They live inside fascia, trim, cabinets, and attic trusses. You'll spot them by tiny ridged pellets under kick-out holes.

pests.name: Dampwood Termites
pests.blurb: Dampwoods show up where wood's stayed wet, rotted eave ends, fence boards touching stucco, or a shower that's leaked for months. Colonies stay small but they mean you've got rot to fix.

Scoop a few wings and a couple dead swarmers into a baggie, note the room and time, and check the garage stem wall and front mulch line for fresh tubes. Indoor swarmers nearly always mean they're already inside the walls.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have termites or flying ants?
faqs.a: Termites have straight waists, straight antennae, and equal-size wings that fall off in piles. Ants have pinched waists and elbowed antennae.

faqs.q: What are mud tubes on my block wall or foundation?
faqs.a: They're soil tunnels subterraneans build over block and stucco to reach wood. Break a small piece, active tubes get rebuilt in days.

faqs.q: Are Formosan termites worse than regular subterranean termites?
faqs.a: Yes, Formosan colonies run bigger and can chew faster, sometimes nesting in roofs without soil contact. Steady bait or a sound liquid zone plus moisture fixes still control them.

faqs.q: Will mulch and irrigation around my home attract termites?
faqs.a: Thick mulch on stucco and daily sprays that keep footers soggy sure help them. Pull mulch back 6 inches, keep soil below siding, and aim heads out.

intro: Cloud. Folks feel embarrassed, but there's no reason to be. These bugs ride in luggage, laundry bags, and used furniture, and a clean house won't stop them.

Ask a provider for a straight answer on what's a bed bug and what's a carpet beetle, plus a plan that fits the room and your turnover schedule. No panic, no judgment, just a careful check and clear next steps.

pests.name: Bed Bugs
pests.blurb: Bed bugs are flat, reddish-brown, apple-seed sized hiders that feed at night. Don't expect winter to slow them down here. One mated female in a suitcase from a Lake Buena Vista turnover can seed a whole bedroom in weeks.

pests.name: Signs of Infestation
pests.blurb: Clustered welts after sleep, black fecal dots and rusty smears on sheets, papery skins stuck in seam folds, a sweet musty odor near a heavy harborage. Look behind the headboard, inside nightstand joints, and where baseboard meets stucco. Daylight checks miss most of it.

pests.name: Common Look-Alikes
pests.blurb: Carpet beetle larvae, spider beetles, booklice from damp baths, and baby German cockroaches all get blamed on bed bugs. Beetle fuzz leaves skins and chews fibers but doesn't bite. Young roaches run fast and hang in kitchens.

sections.heading: How bed bugs ride through the Orlando tourism corridor
body: Tourist turnover is fuel. Cleaners flip the unit, next family checks in, and the bugs have fresh blood and new luggage to ride.

Once they're in town, they move with people and stuff. Visiting relatives, college kids home for break, roommates shifting apartments, all of it helps them hop room to room. Used headboards, mattresses, and couches from Marketplace are another big source.

sections.heading: Heat work compared with conventional bed bug work
body: It kills eggs and active bed bugs together, even where dusts and liquids can't reach.

Conventional work uses targeted liquids, void dusts, and growth regulators with tight prep and a follow-up visit. It costs less, leaves residual control, and suits early catches or rooms full of heat-sensitive gear. A lot of homes land on a blend.

sections.heading: Prep that actually helps, and why store sprays backfire
body: Wash bedding and clothes on hot, dry on high heat, then bag clean loads sealed. Pull beds a few inches off walls, cut clutter around sleeping spots, and make mattress platforms and storage reachable. For rentals, get cleaners, handymen, and managers on the as agreed with the provider so every sleeping area gets opened and checked at once.

Store sprays and foggers push bed bugs deeper into baseboards and next rooms. Foggers coat the air and miss harborages. Light repeat spraying builds resistance and leaves eggs alive. Encasements help for monitoring, but they won't end it alone. Pro equipment, product rotation, and a patient recheck are what break the cycle.

services.h1: Humane Wildlife Removal in Osceola & Orange Counties, Florida
intro: If you're hearing heavy thumps over the lanai at 2 a.m. or waking up to mulch beds plowed like someone ran a tiller through them, that's a normal Tuesday around Kissimmee and St. Cloud. Raccoons, opossums, gray squirrels, and armadillos don't take a season off here. They den in block-home attics, under sheds, and along retention ponds where grubs and trash never run out.
Ask a pest control provider to inspect the affected areas, explain suitable options and confirm pricing, preparation and follow-up in writing. Availability and treatment terms vary by provider.

pests.name: Armadillos
pests.blurb: You'll know armadillos by cone-shaped holes in the turf and mulch kicked across the driveway overnight. They hunt grubs and earthworms after rain and wedge under shed slabs and decks.

pests.name: Opossums
pests.blurb: Opossums love the gap under a shed or lanai enclosure where it's dark and close to cat food. They don't chew much, but they leave greasy rubs, droppings, and that sour trash odor, plus tipped cans.

pests.name: Raccoons
pests.blurb: A mama raccoon will peel back a loose soffit or lift a storm-softened shingle to den right over your bedroom. Then comes night thumping, torn trash, missing citrus, and a latrine in the attic insulation.

pests.name: Gray Squirrels
pests.blurb: Gray squirrels hit in daylight. They run oaks and power lines onto the roof, chew through fascia and stucco returns, and shred insulation into nests. You'll hear rolling and gnawing by morning and find tooth marks on the eave.

pests.name: Flying Squirrels
pests.blurb: Flying squirrels are tiny, nocturnal, and never alone. A colony sounds like soft pattering and squeaks near 11 p.m., with pellet droppings and musky odor in the insulation.

pests.name: Bats
pests.blurb: Bats squeeze through a 3/8-inch gap at the gable or ridge and streak stucco with guano. Florida protects them, so there's no trapping like raccoons.

sections.heading: The usual suspects around Kissimmee attics and yards
body: There's no off-season here. Live near a retention pond, canal, or oak hammock in Buenaventura Lakes or Hunters Creek and you've got roof rats in the citrus, raccoons in the trash, and armadillos working the mulch beds after every afternoon storm. Screen enclosures and lanais help folks, not wildlife. One lifted vent or sun-baked soffit seam is all it takes.

Armadillos leave pitted lawns and soil fanned under the shed. Raccoons thump hard after dark and leave big latrines. Opossums shuffle and stink. Gray squirrels chew in daylight and leave 2-inch holes with tooth marks. Flying squirrels and bats whisper at night and leave pellet droppings or guano streaks on stucco.

sections.heading: Humane work that follows Florida FWC guidance
body: That's usually a shaded live cage trap checked daily or a one-way door over the entry so the animal leaves and can't get back in. It causes a slow death and it kills owls, hawks, and your neighbor's cat when a poisoned animal gets eaten. Traps, droppings, and nesting material get handled with gloves, respirators, and bags, not bare hands.

Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission guidance calls the next step. Raccoons, bats, and a few other species can't legally be hauled to the woods and let go, since that spreads disease and dumps a problem on someone else. In practice that means release on the same property where allowed or humane handling by a pro, plus timed exclusion for bats.

sections.heading: Sealing the house so they stay out
body: Trapping alone buys you a month. The next raccoon will test the same soft soffit. Soffit seams, fascia gaps, roof returns, AC line penetrations, and gable vents get metal, hardware cloth, and sealant that teeth can't chew. Sheds and decks get screened with buried wire. Cut limbs 8 feet off the roof, lock trash lids, and bring pet bowls in at night.

Raccoon latrines and opossum droppings soak insulation and stink up drywall, and that odor pulls in palmetto bugs and roof rats fast in this heat, while soggy fascia invites Formosan termites. You won't wonder what still needs a handyman. It'll be sealed, drier, and quiet.

process.detail: You're getting photos of tracks, droppings, rubs, and chew holes, plus a call on species and if babies are inside.
Traps get checked daily, animals stay calm and covered, and moms with kits get extra care so nobody's left squealing in a wall. No poisons, ever.
Galvanized flashing, quarter-inch hardware cloth, vent guards, and polyurethane sealant on stucco gaps, not foam alone. Armadillo runs get a buried footer.

process.step: Clean up and keep them off
process.detail: You'll leave with a short list. Lock cans, pick citrus, feed pets inside, keep mulch pulled off the slab.

faqs.q: Why can I not just catch a raccoon and release it in the woods?
faqs.a: State rules don't allow moving raccoons off your property, since it spreads disease and they often die or trek back.

faqs.q: How can I tell what is living in my attic?
faqs.a: Listen for timing. Gray squirrels move by day, raccoons and flying squirrels thump and patter at night.

faqs.q: How do you stop armadillos from tearing up my lawn again?
faqs.a: Pick fallen fruit and thin dense cover. Grub killer alone won't stop them.

faqs.q: Do you clean up droppings, odor, and attic mess after removal?
faqs.a: Yes. Sealing at the same time keeps squirrels and rats from moving back in.

spotlight.heading: Removal and prevention options
body: Raccoons and a few other species can't legally be relocated in Florida, so hauling them to the woods isn't an option.
That means covered live traps or one-way doors, daily checks, and metal-backed patches the same visit the attic goes quiet.
points: Shaded live traps, checked daily, no poisons
One-way doors for squirrels and bats in season
Metal, hardware cloth, and sealant on soffits and vents
Photos of entries and a simple prevention list
